title: Privacy Orchestrator: policy-driven access + retention for observability streams
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: Traces, metrics and logs are increasingly surface areas for PII and tenant-sensitive identifiers. Existing ad-hoc scrubbing is baked into individual collectors and post-processing jobs which makes policies inconsistent across tenants and causes operational debt. Scope: build a centralized "Privacy Orchestrator" service that evaluates per-tenant observability policies at ingest and during just-in-time access, drives retention/expiry workflows, enforces RBAC for debugging requests, and emits immutable audit events. Goals: 1) Declarative policy store (per-tenant & per-stream) that covers field masking, TTL/retention, and JIT-unmasking rules. 2) Lightweight tracing hooks that apply masking inline with <2% p50 latency impact for typical requests. 3) Access broker for support/engineering requests that enforces RBAC + time-limited unmasking and records audit logs in the observability audit stream. 4) Retention worker that replaces expired sensitive fields with stable stubs and records provenance so replays and dashboards remain meaningful. This ticket covers the MVP design, proto implementation (staging), integration tests, and a narrow canary rollout plan for Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Policy store deployed to staging with UI + API to CRUD per-tenant masking and retention rules
Ingest pipeline tracing hook applies configured masking to spans/logs before short-term storage in <2% latency overhead
Access broker supports JIT-unmasking requests gated by RBAC and emits audit events to observability.audit with requester, reason, TTL
Retention worker can run a dry-run to produce a report, then replace configured fields with deterministic stubs for at least one test tenant
E2E test that verifies: masked data never appears in low-privilege console views and high-priv views require a logged JIT-unmask event
Migration plan documented and a backfill job template that safely converts existing raw traces into stubbed format
No regressions in latency/error dashboards beyond the agreed threshold (p50 +5ms, p95 +20ms) during canary
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design + security review (2 weeks) - finalize policy schema and threat model
Phase 1: Staging integration (3 weeks) - implement policy store, tracing hook, access broker, retention worker; smoke tests
Phase 2: Canary (3 weeks) - enable for 2 internal tenants + 1 Dedicated customer in us-west, monitor errors/latency and audit trail
Phase 3: Gradual ramp & docs (2 weeks) - publish console controls, run migration for existing tenants who opt-in
Phase 4: GA - announce release + partner enablement
migration_steps: Inventory: run discovery job to enumerate observed fields and PII candidates across traces/logs/metrics
Policy authoring: create conservative default mask rules and retention TTLs for test tenants
Dry-run retention: retention worker runs in report-only mode for 7 days and produces difference metrics
Backfill: run backfill on a snapshot to replace expired fields with deterministic stubs and validate dashboards
Cutover: enable live retention worker and enable policy enforcement on ingest for canary tenants
Post-cutover validation: reconcile audit stream and run comparison queries against dashboards
risks: Runtime overhead: inline masking might add CPU cycles; need microbenchmarks across model-serving paths
False-positives: overly broad masking rules could remove non-sensitive context and break root-cause analysis
Support friction: JIT-unmask UX and approvals could slow investigations if RBAC is too strict
Data permanence: replacing fields reduces ability to replay incidents unless provenance is preserved
Operational complexity: coordinating policy changes across dedicated/private deployments requires rollout tooling
